newsitem.title: BULGARIA: US Defence Secretary Cohen in Bulgaria for talks.
newsitem.headline: US Defence Secretary Cohen in Bulgaria for talks.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen arrived in Bulgaria on Saturday night for talks on European security and NATO with President Petar Stoyanov and other officials at the conclusion of a week-long trip.

Cohen, who flew to the Bulgarian capital Sofia from Ukraine, was greeted at the airport by Defence Minister Georgi Aniniev, who was named earlier this year as the first civilian to head what is still a Soviet-style and equipped military force.
Cohen will hold talks with Stoyanov and other officials on Sunday before flying home to Washington on Monday.
He earlier visited the Czech Republic and Spain.

U.S. officials told reporters travelling with the defence secretary that he would discuss Bulgaria's expressed hope to join NATO and urge the reformist government to pursue recent effective efforts at economic reform, which have dramatically slashed inflation in the small nation from nearly 500 percent to less than 15 percent.
Bulgaria, which during the Cold War was one of Moscow's closest allies, is an active member of NATO'S "Partnership for Peace" military cooperation programme.

The U.S. officials, who asked not to be identified, said Bulgaria still needs to sharply reduce its military and continue economic reforms. They said it was a key country in the Mediterranean region, sharing borders with Greece, Turkey, Macedonia, Romania and Serbia.
